chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Working as A&R man for Jack Lauderdale and passing up Jimmy Forrest
summary: Callender and Lauderdale drive to St. Louis to hear Jimmy Forrest on Clark Terry's tip, but Lauderdale lets "Night Train" get away.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And then I was working for... I was an A&R man for a record company...I can't think of the company...but Jack Lauderdale was the President of the company, and he hired me as an A&R man. So Clark Terry, who was a friend, said, "Hey, I got a guy I want you to hear." So Lauderdale and I get into his Cadillac, and drive back to St. Louis to listen to Jimmy Forrest. So Jimmy Forrest played... I said, "Hey, let's record this guy." (I'll get to the rest in a second.) I said, "Hey, let's record it. This is wonderful." So Lauderdale had some ladies he wanted to see in Chicago, so he said, "No, we can pick up something in Chicago." So we go to Chicago, and two months later, "Night Train" comes out. This was what Lauderdale had passed up. I wanted to do it, and he was too busy to get to see some ladies, and he let that one get by. And I never let him forget it.
Didn't "Night Train" happen after Jimmy Forrest had already worked in Duke's band?
Is that where Clark knew him from, in Duke's band?
Oh, no. Clark knew him before that. You see, Clark is originally from St. Louis...
